I submitted the specification: **features [18, 35] with signs [+1, -1]** (equal-weight long feature 18, short feature 35).

**Summary of approach:**
1. Screened all 40 features individually (sign=+1) to find baseline signal strength — feature 32 (0.257) and 18 (0.232) stood out as strongest.
2. Tried pairwise and triple combinations among the top single features (32, 33, 18, 16, etc.) — these mostly diluted rather than improved the signal, suggesting correlation/redundancy among the top features.
3. Searched for complementary (likely negatively correlated or orthogonal) features to pair with top performers using sign flips — found that feature 18 combined with feature 35 (short) produced a notable improvement to **Sharpe 0.272**, better than any single feature or other combination tested.
4. Tried adding a third feature to this pair in many combinations — none improved on the clean pair, confirming [18, -35] as a locally optimal, parsimonious spec.
5. Verified robustness/stability of the result across sign orderings.

**Prediction rationale:** In-sample Sharpe of 0.272 is modest to begin with, and given this was found via search over many feature combinations (risk of in-sample overfitting / selection bias), I predicted a lower out-of-sample mean Sharpe (0.15) with wide uncertainty (sd 0.25) to reflect the real possibility that this edge partially or fully decays out of sample.
